Part 2&3 地点 PLACE AI 补全经历

Describe a boring place

描述一个无聊的地方

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a boring place

  • Where it is (它在哪里)
  • Who you went there with (你和谁一起去的)
  • What you did there (你在那里做了什么)
  • And explain why you think it is a boring place (并解释为什么你觉得它很无聊)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a boring place

I'd like to describe a place I found incredibly boring: the waiting hall of a big hospital in Shenzhen. It's the outpatient building of a hospital near my home, where my grandfather went for a routine check-up last winter. I went there with my grandfather and my father around eight in the morning, which turned out to be the busiest time of the day. The hall was packed with patients and rows of plastic chairs, with a huge screen showing queue numbers that barely moved. While we waited, there was really nothing to do. My grandfather and father chatted a bit, but I just sat there scrolling my phone, since the Wi-Fi was too weak for video. Every few minutes I'd glance up at the screen, hoping our number would come up, but it kept jumping by only a few places. Honestly, three hours felt like a whole day. The reason it's so boring is that nothing ever happens there. The lighting is flat, the air smells of medicine, and people just sit in silence, staring at their phones or at the wall. There's no conversation, no activity, no sense of time passing, so your mind just goes blank. I remember feeling almost relieved when the check-up finally ended, not because it was good news, but simply because we could leave. All in all, it's the kind of place that makes you realise how precious time is, especially when you're wasting it on a hard plastic chair.

我讲的是深圳一家大医院的门诊候诊大厅，去年冬天陪爷爷去做常规体检。我和爷爷、爸爸早上八点到，大厅挤满病人、一排排塑料椅、叫号屏几乎不动。等待时没什么可做，Wi-Fi 太弱刷不了视频，只能干坐着，三小时像一整天。之所以无聊是因为那里永远什么都不会发生：灯光发白、空气有药味、没人说话，脑子一片空白。检查结束离开时反而松了口气。

Q2Why do most children think education is boring?

I think it's mainly because school education tends to be passive and repetitive. Children sit in class, listen to the teacher, and copy notes, which doesn't engage them the way games or videos do. Another factor is that lessons often feel disconnected from their real interests, which makes it hard for them to see the point. That said, I don't think education itself is boring; it's more about how it's delivered, and I believe more interactive teaching would change that.

主要因为学校教育偏被动、重复：坐着听讲、抄笔记，不像游戏视频那样吸引人；内容又常和兴趣脱节，看不到意义。但教育本身不无聊，是教学方式的问题，互动式教学能改善。

Q3Why aren't young people willing to listen to the experiences of older people?

There are a couple of reasons. For one thing, young people believe the world has changed so much that old advice no longer applies, especially with technology moving so fast. They also prefer discovering things on their own rather than being told what to do, since making mistakes feels like part of growing up. That said, I think this is short-sighted, because older people's experience of relationships and life choices is still relevant, and many come to appreciate it later.

年轻人觉得世界变得太快，老经验不再适用，尤其科技时代；也更想自己摸索而不是被说教。但这有点短视，因为人际关系和人生选择上的经验仍然有用，很多年轻人后来才懂得珍惜。

Q4What can people do when they feel bored?

I think the best approach is to treat boredom as a signal to do something meaningful. People can pick up a hobby, go for a walk, or call a friend, which gets them out of the mental rut quickly. Interestingly, some people now deliberately allow themselves to be bored, because it gives their mind space to wander and come up with creative ideas. I'd say boredom itself isn't the enemy; it's what you do with it that matters.

把无聊当成信号，去做点有意义的事：培养爱好、散步、找朋友聊天，能很快跳出心理低谷。有趣的是现在有人故意让自己无聊，给大脑留白以便产生创意。无聊本身不可怕，怎么利用才重要。

Q5Why are some teachers' classes boring? Are there any solutions?

I'd say boring classes come down to two things: a lack of interaction and relevance. When a teacher just lectures and never asks questions, students' attention drifts, and if the content feels unrelated to their lives, they lose motivation. As for solutions, teachers could introduce discussion, real-world examples, and technology, like quick quizzes or short videos, to break the routine. It takes effort and training, but the payoff is worth it, because an engaged class learns effectively.

无聊的课通常因为缺互动、内容离生活远。老师只顾讲不提问，学生就走神；内容不相关就失去动力。解决：多讨论、加真实案例、用技术（快速小测、短视频）打破单调。这需要老师投入和培训，但值得，因为投入的课堂学得更有效。

Q6待补充

To some extent, yes, we get bored more easily these days. With phones and short videos providing instant entertainment, our attention spans have shrunk, so when we're in a situation without stimulation, like waiting in a queue, it feels unbearable. In the past, people were more used to quiet moments and found simple things enjoyable. However, I wouldn't say this is purely negative; it has also pushed people to seek out new experiences and hobbies, which can enrich their lives.

一定程度是这样。手机和短视频随时提供娱乐，注意力变短，排队这类没刺激的场景就特别难熬；过去的人习惯安静时刻，能从简单事物中找乐趣。但这也不全是坏事，它也推动人们去探索新体验和爱好。
